extra_vocab.en: very interested and active in something you believe in
extra_vocab.note: 用來形容人對工作、目標或活動非常熱心投入，語氣正面、略正式，常見於人物介紹與推薦信。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: zealous 後面常接 about 或 in，再接名詞或 V-ing，不直接接 to V。

example.en: He is a zealous supporter of our recycling program.
example.zh: 他是我們資源回收計畫的熱心支持者。

example.en: The new manager is zealous about improving customer service.
example.zh: 新經理對改善客戶服務非常熱衷。

examples.en: She is a zealous worker who always finishes tasks early.
examples.zh: 她是個熱忱的員工，總是提早完成工作。

examples.en: Our zealous team leader stayed late to prepare the presentation.
examples.zh: 我們熱心的組長留到很晚準備簡報。

examples.en: We thank you for your zealous support of our new project.
examples.zh: 感謝您對我們新專案的熱心支持。

confusable.diff: jealous 是「嫉妒的」，zealous 是「熱心的」，兩個字拼法與發音很像。

example.en: He felt jealous when his coworker got the promotion.
example.zh: 同事獲得升遷時，他感到嫉妒。

similar.diff: 更常見、更口語；zealous 的熱情更強烈、語氣較正式。

example.en: The staff were enthusiastic about the new office plan.
example.zh: 員工們對新的辦公室規劃很感興趣。

similar.diff: eager 強調迫不及待想做某事，常接 to V。

example.en: She is eager to join the sales team.
example.zh: 她很想加入業務團隊。

example.en: He is passionate about helping small businesses grow.
example.zh: 他熱衷於協助小型企業成長。

derived.link: zeal 是詞幹，表示對某件事的強烈熱情。
zealous + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 quick → quickly。

extra_vocab.en: giving a lot of love, time, or effort to someone or something
extra_vocab.note: 形容人對公司、客戶或工作非常忠誠、全心投入，語氣正面，常見於人物介紹與推薦信。devote 是動詞，devoted 多半當形容詞用。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: be devoted to 和 devote A to B 的 to 都是介系詞，後面接名詞或 V-ing，不接原形動詞。

example.en: She devotes two hours every morning to answering customer emails.
example.zh: 她每天早上花兩個小時回覆客戶郵件。

example.en: He is devoting more time to training new staff.
example.zh: 他正投入更多時間訓練新進員工。

example.en: Mr. Chen is a devoted employee who has worked here for years.
example.zh: 陳先生是在這裡工作多年的忠誠員工。

example.en: We will devote more time to customer training.
example.zh: 我們會投入更多時間在客戶培訓上。

example.en: Our devoted customers return to the store every month.
example.zh: 我們的忠實顧客每個月都會回到店裡。

examples.en: The manager thanked the devoted team for their hard work.
examples.zh: 經理感謝這個全心投入的團隊的辛勞。

examples.en: I am devoted to my work and eager to learn.
examples.zh: 我對工作全心投入，並且渴望學習。

examples.en: Thank you for your devoted service to our company.
examples.zh: 感謝您對本公司的忠誠服務。

confusable.diff: devout 是「虔誠的」，多指宗教信仰；devoted 是對人或工作的忠誠投入。

example.en: My devout neighbor goes to the temple every morning.
example.zh: 我虔誠的鄰居每天早上都去廟裡。

similar.diff: 意思幾乎相同，在職場上更常用來形容認真負責的人。

example.en: He is a dedicated engineer who works long hours.
example.zh: 他是個盡心盡力的工程師，工作時間很長。

similar.diff: 強調做出承諾、一定會做到，常接 to。

example.en: The whole team is committed to finishing on time.
example.zh: 整個團隊都承諾會準時完成。

example.en: Loyal customers get a ten percent discount every month.
example.zh: 忠實顧客每個月都享有九折優惠。

derived.link: devote 去掉 e + -ion，變成名詞，像 create → creation。

example.en: The company devotes much money to research each year.
example.zh: 公司每年投入大量資金在研究上。

example.en: Her devoted staff worked all weekend to finish the order.
example.zh: 她忠誠的員工整個週末都在趕這張訂單。

extra_vocab.en: full of energy and ready to be active
extra_vocab.note: 多益徵才廣告與人物介紹常用來形容人有活力、做事積極，如 an energetic team member；語氣正面。

example.en: An energetic team can finish a hard project quickly.
example.zh: 有活力的團隊可以很快完成困難的專案。

example.en: His energetic personality helps him make new clients easily.
example.zh: 他充滿活力的個性讓他很容易結識新客戶。

examples.en: The company wants an energetic person for the sales job.
examples.zh: 公司想找一位有活力的人擔任業務工作。

examples.en: Her energetic speech made everyone excited about the project.
examples.zh: 她充滿活力的演說讓大家對專案感到興奮。

examples.en: Thank you for the energetic presentation you gave this morning.
examples.zh: 謝謝您今天早上充滿活力的簡報。

confusable.diff: energy 是名詞（精力、能源），energetic 是形容詞（有活力的）。
confusable.usage: 要修飾人時用 energetic，不能說 an energy person；energy 是名詞，不可數。

example.en: Solar panels help the factory save energy.
example.zh: 太陽能板幫助工廠節省能源。

similar.diff: lively 常形容氣氛、場面或討論很熱鬧。

example.en: The lively meeting ended with many good ideas.
example.zh: 這場熱烈的會議以許多好點子作結。

similar.diff: active 強調積極參與、常有行動，比 energetic 更中性。

example.en: She stays active in the company sports club.
example.zh: 她在公司運動社團裡很活躍。

example.en: The enthusiastic crowd welcomed the launch of the new product.
example.zh: 熱情的群眾歡迎新產品上市。

derived.link: energy 是詞幹，表示力量與活力。

extra_vocab.en: to speak to a group of listeners
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於會議、頒獎典禮或產品發表會，例如 the CEO addressed the audience；語氣比 talk to 正式。
extra_vocab.pattern: address + the audience + at + 場合
extra_vocab.grammar_note: address 在這裡是及物動詞，後面直接接對象，不加 to：address the audience，不說 address to the audience。

examples.en: The CEO will address the audience at the product launch.
examples.zh: 執行長將在產品發表會上向聽眾致詞。

examples.en: She stood up to address the audience at the annual meeting.
examples.zh: 她起身在年度會議上向聽眾演說。

examples.en: Before the awards began, the host addressed the audience warmly.
examples.zh: 頒獎開始前，主持人親切地向觀眾致詞。

examples.en: Please prepare a short speech to address the audience on Friday.
examples.zh: 請準備一篇短講稿，星期五向聽眾致詞。

similar.diff: 較口語、較一般；address 語氣更正式，常用於正式場合。

example.en: He will speak to the audience after the lunch break.
example.zh: 他會在午休後向聽眾講話。

similar.diff: 強調發表一篇完整的演說，後面要加 to。

example.en: The director will give a speech to the new employees.
example.zh: 主任會對新進員工發表演說。

confusable.diff: address 後面接問題時，意思變成「處理、解決」，而不是「向…演說」。

example.en: We need to address the issue before the next meeting.
example.zh: 我們需要在下次會議前處理這個問題。

extra_vocab.en: to change your opinion because of how someone or something looks
extra_vocab.note: 多益在人資、行銷或消費者行為的文章中常見，例如面試官或顧客容易被外表、包裝左右判斷。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: be influenced by 的介系詞是 by，不是 from 或 with；by 後面接造成影響的事物。

examples.en: Some interviewers are influenced by appearance more than by skills.
examples.zh: 有些面試官受外表影響的程度超過受能力影響。

examples.en: Many shoppers are influenced by appearance when they choose a product.
examples.zh: 許多顧客在選擇產品時會受外觀影響。

examples.en: We should not be influenced by appearance when we choose a supplier.
examples.zh: 我們選擇供應商時不應該受外表影響。

examples.en: The training teaches managers not to be influenced by appearance.
examples.zh: 這個培訓教導主管不要被外表左右。

similar.diff: 範圍更廣，可指任何事物造成的影響，不限於看法或判斷。

example.en: Our sales were affected by the bad weather last month.
example.zh: 我們上個月的銷售受到壞天氣的影響。

similar.diff: 主動表示「以外表來判斷」，主詞是做判斷的人。

example.en: Customers often judge a store by appearance before they enter.
example.zh: 顧客進店前常常以外觀來判斷一家店。

confusable.diff: be impressed by 是「對…印象深刻」，只表示好印象；be influenced by 是「被…左右」，不一定是好印象。

example.en: The clients were impressed by the appearance of the new store.
example.zh: 客戶對新店的外觀印象深刻。

extra_vocab.en: a person who is new to a job or activity
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於課程、軟體說明或徵才廣告，指沒有經驗的人；語氣中性，有時比 beginner 稍正式。

example.en: Novices should read the safety guide before using the machine.
example.zh: 新手在使用機器前應該先閱讀安全指南。

example.en: I am a complete novice when it comes to accounting.
example.zh: 說到會計，我完全是個新手。

example.en: A novice user can set up the printer in minutes.
example.zh: 新手使用者幾分鐘就能設定好印表機。

example.en: The advisor helped the novice investor choose safe funds.
example.zh: 顧問協助這位新手投資人挑選穩健的基金。

examples.en: The class is designed for novices with no sales experience.
examples.zh: 這堂課是為沒有業務經驗的新手設計的。

examples.en: This software is easy to use, even for a novice.
examples.zh: 這個軟體很好用，連新手也能上手。

examples.en: As a novice in marketing, I hope to learn from you.
examples.zh: 身為行銷新手，我希望能向您學習。

confusable.diff: notice 是「通知、注意」，novice 是「新手」，兩個字拼法相近。

example.en: Please give us two weeks' notice before you leave.
example.zh: 離職前請提前兩週通知我們。

similar.diff: 更口語、更常用；novice 稍正式，常強調缺乏經驗。

example.en: This course is for beginners who have never used Excel.
example.zh: 這門課是給沒用過 Excel 的初學者。

similar.diff: 指剛加入團體或公司的人，不一定沒有經驗。

example.en: We give each newcomer a short tour of the office.
example.zh: 我們帶每位新人簡短參觀辦公室。

example.en: The company hired an expert to fix the network problem.
example.zh: 公司聘請了一位專家來解決網路問題。

example.en: Every trainee works with a senior staff member for a month.
example.zh: 每位受訓人員都會跟著資深員工工作一個月。

extra_vocab.en: the money you get from your job, or the check that shows it
extra_vocab.note: 美式用語，多益常見於人資、財務與勞動相關話題，如 monthly paycheck、paycheck deductions；口語中常泛指「薪水」。

example.en: Our paychecks arrive on the last working day of each month.
example.zh: 我們的薪水在每個月最後一個工作日發放。

example.en: Part-time staff also get a paycheck every two weeks.
example.zh: 兼職人員每兩週也會領到薪水。

example.en: His monthly paycheck goes straight into his bank account.
example.zh: 他的月薪直接存進銀行帳戶。

collocations.zh: 月光族、靠每期薪水過活

example.en: Many young workers live paycheck to paycheck in big cities.
example.zh: 許多年輕上班族在大城市過著月光的生活。

examples.en: Please check the amount on your paycheck carefully.
examples.zh: 請仔細核對薪資單上的金額。

examples.en: The bank wants a copy of my latest paycheck for the loan.
examples.zh: 銀行要求我提供最近一期薪資證明來辦貸款。

examples.en: Your paycheck will be late because of the bank holiday.
examples.zh: 因為銀行假日，您的薪水會晚一點發放。

confusable.diff: payroll 指公司發薪的整體作業或部門，paycheck 是個人實際拿到的薪水。

example.en: The payroll department pays all employees on the last day of the month.
example.zh: 薪資部門在每月最後一天發薪給所有員工。

similar.diff: 指固定的月薪或年薪，語氣較正式；paycheck 指實際領到的那一筆。

example.en: Her salary is paid on the twenty-fifth of every month.
example.zh: 她的薪水在每個月二十五日發放。

similar.diff: 指附在薪水旁、列出扣除項目的薪資明細單。

example.en: Your pay stub lists tax and insurance deductions clearly.
example.zh: 您的薪資明細清楚列出稅金與保險的扣款。

example.en: The factory raised the hourly wage for all workers.
example.zh: 工廠調高了所有工人的時薪。

example.en: Our monthly income rose after the new contract.
example.zh: 簽了新合約後，我們的月收入增加了。

extra_vocab.en: the ability to push yourself to work without being told
extra_vocab.note: 多益徵才廣告與人物介紹常見，常和 teamwork、communication skills 並列，表示不需要主管催促也會主動把事做好。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: self-motivation 是不可數名詞，不加 a 或 s；要形容人時用形容詞 self-motivated。

example.en: Applicants should show self-motivation in their cover letters.
example.zh: 應徵者應該在求職信中展現自發性。

example.en: Some new staff lack self-motivation and wait for instructions.
example.zh: 有些新進員工缺乏自發性，只會等指示。

example.en: Working from home requires a lot of self-motivation.
example.zh: 在家工作需要很強的自我激勵。

examples.en: This job needs strong self-motivation and good time management.
examples.zh: 這份工作需要很強的自發性與良好的時間管理。

examples.en: My self-motivation helped me finish the course while working full time.
examples.zh: 我的自我激勵讓我在全職工作的同時完成了課程。

examples.en: Her self-motivation impressed the manager during the first month.
examples.zh: 她的自發性在第一個月就讓經理印象深刻。

confusable.diff: self-confidence 是「自信」，self-motivation 是「自我激勵、主動做事的動力」。

example.en: Self-confidence helps you speak clearly in front of clients.
example.zh: 自信能幫助你在客戶面前清楚表達。

similar.diff: 強調不用別人交代就主動採取行動。

example.en: She showed initiative by fixing the problem herself.
example.zh: 她主動親自解決了這個問題。

similar.diff: 指想達成目標的強烈動力，語氣更口語。

example.en: His drive to succeed impressed the whole team.
example.zh: 他想成功的幹勁讓整個團隊印象深刻。

example.en: Good teamwork helped us meet the deadline last week.
example.zh: 良好的團隊合作幫助我們上週趕上了截止日。

derived.link: motivate 是詞幹，表示給人做事的動力。
motivate 去掉 e + -ion，變成名詞，像 create → creation。
motivate + -ed，形容人「被激勵的」，像 excited、interested。
